title: Körner–Malvenuto's maximal colliding-permutations conjecture
statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$. Two permutations $\pi_1,\pi_2$ of $[n]$ are **colliding** if there is an index $i\in[n]$ such that $|\pi_1(i)-\pi_2(i)|=1$.

**Körner–Malvenuto's conjecture.** The maximal number of pairwise colliding permutations of $[n]$ is

$$
\binom{n}{\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor}.
$$

The paper recalls this earlier extremal question as motivation for studying graph-different Hamiltonian paths. Its status is not specified in the source.
source_name: István Kovács and Dániel Soltész, “Triangle-different Hamiltonian paths”, arXiv:1608.05237 (2016).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1106.0725](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0725), [arXiv:0712.1442](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1442).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.05237

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2016). “The maximal number of $C_4$- or $K_4$-different Hamiltonian paths is also an open question at the time, even the correct order of magnitude is unknown.”
